title: tcp: Fix handling of retransmission for reassembly
description:
When reassemble_ooo is set, we can do a better job determining
if a segment is retransmitted or not from the reassembler perspective,
which is different than what TCP sequence analysis determines, which
is retransmission from the sender's perspective.

This also allows us to have a good way of dealing with retransmission
but with additional data.

This only works when reassembling out of order is set. Without it,
we fall back to the old method of detecting retransmissions, which
has a harder time with the edge cases.

Fix #17406, fix #15993, fix #13388, fix #13523.

notes.body:
added 5 commits
  • 00c14e98...fce0b28a - 4 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 7cfef49e - tcp: Fix handling of retransmission for reassembly
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7949/diffs?diff_id=471673094&start_sha=00c14e9874292b6bc5cdc57c66965470c7e90afa)

This is correct for when the out-of-order preference is enabled, and in-order delivery to the subdissector is guaranteed. The problem with enabling that preference is that, like real TCP processing, a missing packet that is never retransmitted causes blocking.

It's still worth investigating what improvements can be done in the cases with that preference has to be set to false because there are missing packets never retransmitted. Right now it uses TCP analysis results, which are not necessarily correct from the reassembly perspective.

added 10 commits
  • 7cfef49e...bed5b0e0 - 9 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • f3df91b9 - tcp: Fix handling of retransmission for reassembly
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7949/diffs?diff_id=473215652&start_sha=7cfef49e4fb0acb51df5256b8ece00eb08d396a4)

I don't believe this actually fixes the #15993 - for instance, [tcp-ooo.pcapng](/uploads/012bc1a40fc084567d2749f72e4e27a0/tcp-ooo.pcapng) still shows packet 40 as being segment not captured and 41 as a retransmission.

![Screen_Shot_2022-08-30_at_6.17.47_PM](/uploads/14949f7850acef38d70551066ba5ac68/Screen_Shot_2022-08-30_at_6.17.47_PM.png)

It fixes the "breaks reassembly" that is the title of the bug. It does not fix the related "TCP Analysis marks some segments as Retransmissions when they are actually Out-Of-Order, and vice versa" issue.

Even with that fixed, packet 40 would still show as "previous segment not captured" because TCP analysis is done sequentially.

Though it only fixes breaking reassembly when "reassemble out-of-order" is on, but that is necessary in order to handle TLS. There are some dissectors that can work fine when they get complete PDUs out of order, but TLS is not one of them (at least when dissecting.)

Bugs #13843, ~~#16913,~~ #10725, and possibly others, all address the "some segments are marked as retranmissions when they are actually out-of-order, and vice versa" issue. This MR didn't close those. (Edit: The second one is about IP retransmission, but the first and third cover both directions of the TCP analysis issue.)

changes_data.diff:
@@ -621,15 +621,17 @@ class case_dissect_tcp(subprocesstest.SubprocessTestCase):
         # H - first time that the start of the MSP is delivered
         self.assertIn('3\t6\t[TCP Out-Of-Order]', lines[2])
         self.assertIn('[TCP segment of a reassembled PDU]', lines[2])
-        # H - first retransmission.
-        self.assertIn('4\t\t', lines[3])
-        self.assertNotIn('[TCP segment of a reassembled PDU]', lines[3])
+        # H - first retransmission. Because this is before the reassembly
+        # completes we can add it to the reassembly
+        self.assertIn('4\t6\t[TCP Out-Of-Order]', lines[3])
+        self.assertIn('[TCP segment of a reassembled PDU]', lines[3])
         # 1 - continue reassembly
         self.assertIn('5\t6\t[TCP Out-Of-Order]', lines[4])
         self.assertIn('[TCP segment of a reassembled PDU]', lines[4])
         # 3 - finish reassembly
         self.assertIn('6\t\tPUT /0 HTTP/1.1', lines[5])
-        # H - second retransmission.
+        # H - second retransmission. This is after the reassembly completes
+        # so we do not add it to the ressembly (but throw a ReassemblyError.)
         self.assertIn('7\t\t', lines[6])
         self.assertNotIn('[TCP segment of a reassembled PDU]', lines[6])
